Describe how Dijkstra's algorithm uses the edge weights of the given graph to update the shortest known distances from vertex A.
Determine why the shortest path from A to B passes through C rather than using the direct edge A–B = 4, and identify which other shortest distances from A depend on that detour.
Validate the proposed shortest distances A = 0, B = 3, C = 2, D = 8, and E = 10 for the given graph, justifying the result with the available paths.

Design a change to one edge weight in the graph with edges A–B = 4, A–C = 2, B–C = 1, B–D = 5, C–D = 8, C–E = 10, and D–E = 2 that changes the shortest path from A to E, and show the new shortest distances from vertex A.
Calculate the voltage regulation of a single-phase transformer when its no-load secondary voltage is 240 V and its full-load secondary voltage is 228 V at the specified power factor.
State the formula for transformer voltage regulation and identify the no-load and full-load secondary voltage quantities.
Interpret the change from a no-load secondary voltage of 240 V to a full-load secondary voltage of 228 V as the transformer's voltage regulation.

Determine why the voltage regulation of the transformer differs depending on whether its voltage drop is expressed relative to the 240 V no-load voltage or the 228 V full-load voltage, and identify which convention gives the larger value.

Verify whether the reported voltage regulation of 5% is correct when regulation is expressed relative to the no-load secondary voltage, using the no-load secondary voltage of 240 V and full-load secondary voltage of 228 V, and justify the convention used.

Develop a tap-setting proposal for the transformer that would raise its full-load secondary voltage towards its 240 V no-load value, using the stated no-load voltage of 240 V and full-load voltage of 228 V at the specified power factor to determine the voltage boost required.

Evaluate the fairness of an employee performance appraisal in which a supervisor assesses employees solely on their most recent month's performance, although the appraisal is intended to cover the entire year.
Define performance appraisal.
Explain why assessing only the most recent month's performance may not represent an employee's performance throughout the entire year.

An employee's monthly performance ratings for the year average 3.8 out of 5, but the rating for the most recent month is 2.5. Apply the stated appraisal practice to determine the annual rating the supervisor would give, and compare it with the rating a full-year assessment would give.
Examine the relationship between the appraisal period and the supervisor's evidence selection to identify the source of potential unfairness.
Develop a revised appraisal approach for the stated annual evaluation that addresses the reliance on only the most recent month's performance while retaining the full-year assessment scope.
Explain how ethanoic acid reacts with ethanol in the presence of concentrated sulfuric acid to produce ethyl ethanoate and water.
Name the products formed when a carboxylic acid reacts with an alcohol in the presence of an acid catalyst.
Complete the balanced chemical equation for the reaction between ethanoic acid and ethanol in the presence of concentrated sulfuric acid.
Examine the structural changes between ethanoic acid and ethanol and the product ethyl ethanoate to identify how the ester linkage forms during the reaction.
Judge whether the proposed equation CH_3COOH + C_2H_5OH ⇌ CH_3COOC_2H_5 + H_2O correctly represents the stated esterification reaction.

Propose a modified reaction set-up for the esterification of ethanoic acid with ethanol that increases the yield of ethyl ethanoate, and explain how the concentrated sulfuric acid and the removal of water shift the equilibrium in your design.

Assess whether a seller's statement that a used vehicle has never been involved in an accident constitutes actionable misrepresentation when the seller knows the statement is false and the buyer relies on it when purchasing the vehicle.
Define misrepresentation and identify the elements relevant to the seller's statement about the vehicle's accident history.
Explain how a false statement about a vehicle's accident history may influence a buyer's decision to enter into a contract.
Apply the elements of fraudulent misrepresentation to the stated vehicle sale to determine which remedies are available to the buyer.
Examine the relationship between the seller's knowledge of the vehicle's accident history, the false statement, and the buyer's reliance in the stated transaction.
Draft a claim for the buyer in the stated vehicle-sale scenario, specifying the elements of misrepresentation to be pleaded, the supporting facts, and the remedy sought.
Calculate the inverse of the matrix A=[[2, 1], [5, 3]] using the determinant and adjugate method.
State the determinant and adjugate formula used to calculate the inverse of a nonsingular square matrix.
Describe how the determinant and adjugate of A=[[2, 1], [5, 3]] are used to obtain its inverse.
Investigate why the inverse of A=[[2, 1], [5, 3]] has integer entries, and explain what would happen to the inverse if the determinant of A were zero.
Verify whether [[3, -1], [-5, 2]] is the correct inverse of A=[[2, 1], [5, 3]] by checking the matrix product AA^(-1).

Construct a different 2×2 matrix with the same determinant as A=[[2, 1], [5, 3]], determine its inverse by the determinant and adjugate method, and show that each matrix multiplied by its inverse gives the identity matrix.

Analyze the irrigation schedule of a maize field with a root-zone available water capacity of 120 mm, current root-zone water depletion of 60 mm, and an allowable depletion fraction of 0.5 to determine whether irrigation is required.
Define root-zone available water capacity and allowable depletion fraction in irrigation scheduling.
Explain how the allowable depletion fraction of 0.5 relates to the 120 mm available water capacity and the 60 mm current depletion in the maize field.
Calculate the allowable root-zone water depletion and determine whether irrigation is required when the current depletion is 60 mm.
Should the maize field be irrigated at a current depletion of 60 mm, given its 120 mm available water capacity and 0.5 allowable depletion fraction? Justify your decision.

Design an irrigation schedule for the maize field, using its root-zone available water capacity of 120 mm, current depletion of 60 mm, and allowable depletion fraction of 0.5, that specifies when irrigation should be applied and the depth of water needed to refill the root zone.

Analyze a proposed university attendance-management system in terms of technical feasibility, economic feasibility, and operational feasibility, considering the availability of existing computers, implementation costs, and staff readiness.
Outline what technical, economic, and operational feasibility each mean in information-system development.
Explain how existing computers, implementation costs, and staff readiness relate to the technical, economic, and operational feasibility of the proposed attendance-management system.

Apply the three feasibility dimensions to the proposed university attendance-management system by stating whether the availability of existing computers, the implementation costs, and staff readiness each concern technical, economic, or operational feasibility.
Assess whether the proposed university attendance-management system is feasible based on its existing computer resources, implementation costs, and staff readiness.

Plan the implementation of the proposed university attendance-management system so that it addresses the technical, economic, and operational feasibility concerns arising from the existing computers, implementation costs, and staff readiness.
Calculate the magnetic force on a straight conductor of length 0.5 m carrying a current of 4 A in a uniform magnetic field of 0.2 T when the conductor is perpendicular to the magnetic field.
State the equation for the magnetic force on a current-carrying conductor and identify the physical quantities in the equation.
Clarify why the perpendicular orientation of the 0.5 m conductor carrying 4 A in a 0.2 T magnetic field produces the maximum magnetic force for the given current, length, and field strength.

Determine how the magnetic force on the 0.5 m conductor carrying 4 A in a 0.2 T field would change as the conductor is rotated away from the perpendicular toward the field direction, and explain why only the perpendicular component of the field matters.
Is a calculated magnetic force of 0.4 N correct for the 0.5 m conductor carrying 4 A perpendicular to the 0.2 T magnetic field? Show the check that supports your answer.

Design a modified conductor arrangement that doubles the magnetic force on the 0.5 m conductor carrying 4 A in the uniform 0.2 T field while keeping the conductor perpendicular to the field, specifying which quantities are changed and the resulting force.
Compare the mass-per-length and length-per-mass yarn count systems by interpreting a yarn labelled 30 tex and another labelled Ne 30.
Define the tex and English cotton count (Ne) systems of yarn numbering.
Explain how the 30 tex and Ne 30 labels represent yarn fineness using different mass–length relationships.
Use the relationship Ne = 590.5/tex to convert the 30 tex yarn to the English cotton count and the Ne 30 yarn to tex, and state which yarn is finer.
Assess whether the statement that 30 tex and Ne 30 represent the same yarn fineness is correct, considering the definitions of both count systems.

Design a labelling and ordering guide for a spinning mill that sells to buyers using tex and to buyers using Ne, including a conversion rule, worked labels for the 30 tex and Ne 30 yarns, and guidance on which count to quote for each market.

Evaluate the suitability of a cyclone separator for removing particulate matter from an industrial exhaust stream when the supplied operating conditions indicate a high gas flow rate and particles of relatively large diameter.
Identify the principal components of a cyclone separator and state its basic particle-separation principle.
Explain how centrifugal action separates relatively large particles from an industrial exhaust stream in a cyclone separator.

Predict, using the cyclone cut-diameter relationship in which the cut diameter decreases as inlet velocity increases, how raising the inlet velocity at the stated high gas flow rate would change the collection of the relatively large particles.
Examine how gas flow rate and particle diameter influence the separation behaviour of the cyclone separator under the stated operating conditions.

Design a particulate-control system for the stated industrial exhaust stream with a high gas flow rate and relatively large particles, specifying the cyclone arrangement, such as multiple cyclones in parallel, and any downstream unit required.
Analyze the following requirements traceability relationships to identify whether every stated software requirement is connected to at least one corresponding test case.
Define requirements traceability and identify the purpose of linking software requirements to test cases.
Explain how the listed test cases provide verification coverage for requirements R1, R2, R3, and R4.
Calculate the percentage of the four listed requirements that are covered by at least one test case.
Assess whether the supplied traceability relationships provide complete test coverage for all four requirements, justifying the conclusion using the listed mappings.

Design additional test cases that close the gaps in the requirements traceability relationships so that every requirement is connected to at least one test case, and present the completed traceability matrix.

Apply Bernoulli's equation to calculate the pressure at point 2 in a horizontal pipe when the pressure at point 1 is 200 kPa, the fluid velocity at point 1 is 2 m/s, the velocity at point 2 is 4 m/s, and the fluid density is 1,000 kg/m³. Assume steady, incompressible, frictionless flow.
State Bernoulli's equation for steady, incompressible, frictionless flow and identify its pressure, velocity, and elevation terms.
Explain how an increase in fluid velocity from 2 m/s to 4 m/s affects pressure in the stated horizontal pipe under Bernoulli's principle.

Determine why the pressure drop between points 1 and 2 depends on the difference of the squared velocities rather than on the velocity difference itself, and explain the consequence of doubling the velocity from 2 m/s to 4 m/s.
Check the proposed pressure at point 2 of 194 kPa against the given pressure, velocities, fluid density, and horizontal-pipe assumption, and decide whether it is correct.

Design a modified diameter at point 2 of the horizontal pipe, with 200 kPa and 2 m/s at point 1 and a fluid density of 1,000 kg/m³, that keeps the pressure at point 2 above a chosen minimum, using Bernoulli's equation and continuity for steady, incompressible flow.
Calculate the therapeutic index of a drug when its median lethal dose (LD50) is 500 mg/kg and its median effective dose (ED50) is 50 mg/kg, and interpret the resulting value.
Define therapeutic index and state the relationship between LD50 and ED50 used to calculate it.
Interpret what an LD50 of 500 mg/kg and an ED50 of 50 mg/kg indicate about the separation between the drug's median lethal and median effective doses.
Determine why two drugs with the same therapeutic index of 10 could differ in safety, relating this to the fact that an LD50 of 500 mg/kg and an ED50 of 50 mg/kg summarize only median responses.
Verify whether a reported therapeutic index of 10 is correct using the given LD50 of 500 mg/kg and ED50 of 50 mg/kg, and assess what the value indicates.
Design a dosing guideline for the drug with an LD50 of 500 mg/kg and an ED50 of 50 mg/kg that specifies a recommended dose range and monitoring requirements based on its therapeutic index.

Calculate the simple money multiplier and the resulting maximum change in the money supply when the required reserve ratio is 20% and the banking system receives a new deposit of Tk. 100,000, assuming banks lend all excess reserves and the public holds no cash.
State the formula for the simple money multiplier and identify the required reserve ratio used in the calculation.
Describe how a required reserve ratio of 20% determines the proportion of each deposit that banks must retain and how lending excess reserves creates money.

Analyze why the successive rounds of lending from the initial Tk. 100,000 deposit become smaller at a 20% reserve requirement, and determine why their sum approaches a finite total rather than growing without limit.
Validate a maximum change in the money supply of Tk. 500,000 for the 20% reserve ratio and the initial Tk. 100,000 deposit under the stated assumptions.

Design a reserve-requirement proposal that would limit the maximum change in the money supply from the new Tk. 100,000 deposit to a chosen target, using the 20% required reserve ratio as the baseline and keeping the stated assumptions that banks lend all excess reserves and the public holds no cash.
Analyze the suitability of a flat roof and a pitched roof for a building in a region receiving heavy rainfall, considering rainwater drainage, roof slope, and construction requirements.
Identify the principal characteristics of flat and pitched roof systems, including their typical roof slopes and drainage arrangements.
Relate roof slope to rainwater drainage in flat and pitched roof systems in a region receiving heavy rainfall.
Calculate the rise of a pitched roof that gives a 30° slope over a horizontal half-span of 5 m, and state why such a slope suits a region receiving heavy rainfall.
Recommend the roof system for the stated heavy-rainfall region, justifying the choice by rainwater drainage, roof slope, and construction requirements.
Develop a roof for a building in the stated heavy-rainfall region that specifies its slope, drainage arrangement, and construction details, and justify each choice.

Evaluate whether a restriction on a public demonstration is justified when the stated reasons are protection of public order and prevention of disruption, while considering the constitutional protection of freedom of expression under the applicable legal framework.
Name the constitutional right engaged when a public demonstration is restricted.
Explain the relationship between constitutional protection of freedom of expression and restrictions imposed to protect public order under an applicable legal framework.
Apply the proportionality test (legitimate aim, suitability, necessity, and balance) to a total ban on a peaceful demonstration that is imposed to prevent traffic disruption.
Examine the tension between the demonstrators' freedom of expression and the stated public-order reasons for restricting the demonstration.

Construct a structured constitutional argument addressing the restriction on the public demonstration that incorporates freedom of expression and the stated public-order considerations under the applicable legal framework.
Calculate the dynamic power dissipation of a CMOS inverter operating at a supply voltage of 1.8 V, switching frequency of 100 MHz, effective load capacitance of 10 pF, and activity factor of 0.5.
Write the dynamic power-dissipation equation for a CMOS inverter and name each of its variables.
Describe how the supply voltage, switching frequency, effective load capacitance, and activity factor influence the dynamic power dissipation of the stated CMOS inverter.

Determine which of the 1.8 V supply, 100 MHz switching frequency, 10 pF load capacitance, and 0.5 activity factor gives the greatest reduction in dynamic power for a given percentage change, and explain why.
Is a reported dynamic power dissipation of 0.81 mW correct for the stated CMOS inverter parameters? Check it with the dynamic power equation P=αC_LV_DD^2f.

Design low-power operating changes for the CMOS inverter operating at 1.8 V, 100 MHz, 10 pF effective load capacitance, and an activity factor of 0.5 that halve its dynamic power dissipation, specifying which parameters are changed and the resulting power.
Calculate the patient's net fluid balance over an 8-hour shift when oral intake is 600 mL, intravenous intake is 500 mL, urine output is 800 mL, and other measured fluid output is 100 mL.
Recall what fluid intake, fluid output, and net fluid balance mean in patient monitoring.
Describe how oral and intravenous intake and urine and other measured output contribute to the patient's net fluid balance during the 8-hour shift.

Determine whether the patient's net fluid balance over the 8-hour shift is driven more by the intravenous intake or by the urine output, and identify which unmeasured losses could make the recorded balance misleading.
Verify whether a reported positive net fluid balance of 200 mL is correct using the patient's stated intake and output measurements.

Develop a fluid-management plan for the patient's next 8-hour shift, based on the current shift's 600 mL oral intake, 500 mL intravenous intake, 800 mL urine output, and 100 mL other measured output, specifying intake targets that would bring the net fluid balance to zero.
Calculate the total manufacturing cost of Job 105 when direct materials are Tk. 20,000, direct labour is Tk. 15,000, and manufacturing overhead is applied at 80% of direct labour cost.
Name the principal components of total manufacturing cost under job order costing.
Explain how direct materials, direct labour, and overhead applied at 80% of direct labour cost contribute to the total manufacturing cost of Job 105.

Analyze how the 80% overhead application rate makes direct labour cost affect Job 105's total manufacturing cost twice over, and explain why a given increase in direct labour raises the total cost by more than the increase itself.
Judge whether a reported total manufacturing cost of Tk. 47,000 is correct for Job 105 using the stated direct materials, direct labour, and overhead application rate.

Develop a quotation for Job 105 based on its direct materials of Tk. 20,000, direct labour of Tk. 15,000, and manufacturing overhead applied at 80% of direct labour cost, proposing a selling price that includes a chosen profit margin.

Analyze the energy transfer in a food chain consisting of grass, grasshoppers, frogs, and snakes when the grass contains 10,000 kJ of available energy and the 10% energy-transfer rule applies at each trophic-level transfer.
State the 10% energy-transfer rule and identify the trophic levels represented by grass, grasshoppers, frogs, and snakes.
Explain how the 10% energy-transfer rule determines the energy available to grasshoppers, frogs, and snakes from the initial 10,000 kJ in grass.
Calculate the energy available at each trophic level in the given food chain using the 10% energy-transfer rule.
Verify whether the proposed energy values of 1,000 kJ for grasshoppers, 100 kJ for frogs, and 10 kJ for snakes are consistent with the 10% transfer rule and the initial 10,000 kJ in grass.

Design a modified food chain with the same grass base of 10,000 kJ that would increase the energy available to its top consumer under the 10% energy-transfer rule, and show the available energy at each trophic level of your design.

Interpret the following tensile-test results for a material specimen: an applied tensile force of 20 kN acts on an original cross-sectional area of 100 mm², and the specimen extends by 0.5 mm from an original gauge length of 100 mm. Calculate the engineering stress and engineering strain.
Define engineering stress and engineering strain and state their respective formulas.

Explain how the applied tensile force of 20 kN, original cross-sectional area of 100 mm², extension of 0.5 mm, and original gauge length of 100 mm are used to characterize the specimen's tensile behaviour.

Examine why engineering stress and strain are computed from the original area and gauge length rather than the instantaneous ones, and explain how this choice would misstate the material's behaviour at large extensions.
Verify whether the reported engineering stress of 200 MPa and engineering strain of 0.005 are correct using the given tensile-test measurements.

Propose a revised tensile specimen for the same material and 20 kN applied force that would halve the engineering stress produced on the 100 mm² original cross-sectional area, and predict the corresponding strain over a 100 mm gauge length assuming linear elastic behaviour.

Determine the open-loop transfer function and characteristic equation for a unity-feedback control system with forward-path transfer function G(s)=K/(s(s+2)(s+4)), and use the characteristic equation to identify the closed-loop pole locations for K=8.
State the characteristic equation of a unity-feedback control system in terms of its open-loop transfer function.
Describe how the forward-path transfer function G(s)=K/(s(s+2)(s+4)) determines the characteristic equation of the unity-feedback system.
Determine how each open-loop pole at s = 0, −2, and −4 shapes the root locus of G(s)=K/(s(s+2)(s+4)), and identify the gain at which the closed-loop poles reach the imaginary axis.
Assess whether the unity-feedback system with G(s)=K/(s(s+2)(s+4)) is stable at K=8 by examining its characteristic equation, and justify the conclusion using the Routh–Hurwitz criterion.

Design a gain-selection proposal for the unity-feedback system with G(s)=K/(s(s+2)(s+4)) that keeps all closed-loop poles in the left half-plane, using the characteristic equation to identify the stable gain range, and justify the chosen operating gain relative to K=8.

Prepare a bank reconciliation statement using the following information: the cash-book balance is Tk. 25,000, deposits of Tk. 5,000 have not yet been credited by the bank, and cheques issued for Tk. 3,000 have not yet been presented for payment. Assume there are no other reconciling items.
Specify what a bank reconciliation statement is and what deposits in transit and outstanding cheques are.
Why do deposits of Tk. 5,000 not yet credited and cheques of Tk. 3,000 not yet presented cause the cash-book and bank-statement balances to differ?
Distinguish the reconciling item that raises the bank-statement balance relative to the Tk. 25,000 cash-book balance from the one that lowers it, and explain why each arises from timing alone.
Determine whether a reconciled bank-statement balance of Tk. 27,000 is correct from the cash-book balance and the two stated reconciling items, and justify the conclusion.

Design a month-end reconciliation procedure for the business that detects deposits not yet credited and cheques not yet presented, illustrated with the Tk. 25,000 cash-book balance, Tk. 5,000 uncredited deposits, and Tk. 3,000 unpresented cheques.

Analyze the following CNC machining sequence for a cylindrical workpiece to determine how facing, turning, and parting operations contribute to the final component: the workpiece is first faced to establish a flat end, then turned to a specified diameter, and finally parted to separate the finished component.
Define facing, turning, and parting operations in CNC machining.
Explain how facing establishes a flat end, turning produces the specified diameter, and parting separates the finished cylindrical component.
Determine the effect of each operation in the stated machining sequence on the cylindrical workpiece.
Assess whether the stated sequence of facing, turning, and parting is appropriate for producing the described cylindrical component.
Plan a CNC machining process for the stated cylindrical workpiece that adds the tool selection and cutting order needed to achieve the specified diameter with the fewest set-ups.

Test whether the population mean differs from 50 at the 5% significance level using a sample mean of 53, a known population standard deviation of 10, and a sample size of 100. Assume the population is normally distributed.
Specify the null and alternative hypotheses for a two-tailed one-sample z-test and the formula for its test statistic.
Describe how the sample mean of 53, hypothesized population mean of 50, known standard deviation of 10, and sample size of 100 are used to test the population mean.
Examine the difference between the sample mean and hypothesized population mean in relation to the standard error to determine the evidence provided by the sample.
Validate the decision to reject the null hypothesis at the 5% significance level by comparing the calculated z-statistic with the two-tailed critical value of approximately ±1.96.

Design a one-sample z-test study for the same population (σ=10, hypothesized mean 50, 5% significance level, two-tailed) that would detect a 3-unit difference in the mean with a chosen power, determining the required sample size and comparing it with n=100.
Calculate the absorbance of a solution with a molar absorptivity of 150 L mol⁻¹ cm⁻¹, concentration of 0.002 mol/L, and cuvette path length of 1 cm using the Beer–Lambert law.
State the Beer–Lambert law and identify the roles of absorbance, molar absorptivity, concentration, and path length.
Explain how the molar absorptivity of 150 L mol⁻¹ cm⁻¹, concentration of 0.002 mol/L, and path length of 1 cm determine the solution's absorbance.
Determine why doubling either the concentration or the path length of the stated solution doubles its absorbance, and explain why the Beer–Lambert law may stop holding at high concentrations.
Verify whether the reported absorbance of 0.30 is correct using the stated molar absorptivity, concentration, and path length.

Formulate a dilution plan for the solution with molar absorptivity 150 L mol⁻¹ cm⁻¹ and concentration 0.002 mol/L, measured in a 1 cm cuvette, that brings its absorbance into a chosen measurement range, specifying the dilution factor and the expected absorbance.

Apply the distance-vector routing update rule to determine router A's shortest known distances when its current distance to destination D is 8, router B advertises a distance of 3 to D, and the link cost from A to B is 2.
State the distance-vector routing update equation and identify the roles of link cost and a neighbouring router's advertised distance.
Describe how router A combines its link cost to router B with B's advertised distance to destination D when updating its routing table.

Determine under what condition on router B's advertised distance router A would keep its current distance of 8 to destination D, given the A–B link cost of 2, and explain why A cannot verify B's advertisement.
Verify whether updating router A's distance to destination D from 8 to 5 is correct using the stated link cost and advertised distance.

Design a link-cost condition between routers A and B under which router A keeps its current distance of 8 to destination D instead of routing through B, which advertises a distance of 3, and state the condition on the A–B link cost.
Calculate the plasticity index of a soil sample when its liquid limit is 48% and its plastic limit is 22%, and classify the soil according to its plasticity index.
Define liquid limit, plastic limit, and plasticity index in soil mechanics.
Explain how the liquid limit of 48% and plastic limit of 22% determine the range of water content over which the soil behaves plastically.

Infer whether the soil with a liquid limit of 48% and a plastic limit of 22% plots above or below the A-line on a plasticity chart, and explain what its position indicates about its clay or silt character.

Is the reported plasticity index of 26% correct for the stated liquid limit and plastic limit, and is describing the soil as highly plastic justified by Burmister's ranges (PI 20–40% indicates high plasticity)? Give reasons for both judgements.

Develop a soil-improvement proposal for the soil with a liquid limit of 48% and a plastic limit of 22%, specifying how its plasticity characteristics should be modified for use as a construction material and the target plasticity-index range you select.

Analyze the following transactions to determine whether each belongs to the current account or financial account of a country's balance of payments: export of garments worth USD 2 million, receipt of USD 500,000 from overseas workers, and foreign direct investment of USD 3 million.
Name the main accounts of a country's balance of payments.
Explain why exports of goods and workers' remittances are recorded differently from foreign direct investment in the balance of payments.

Calculate the total current-account credit and the financial-account inflow that result from the USD 2 million garment export, the USD 500,000 remittance from overseas workers, and the USD 3 million foreign direct investment.
Assess whether the classification of the garment export and overseas-worker remittance under the current account and foreign direct investment under the financial account is correct.

Design a set of additional transactions that would offset the stated transactions' effect on the current account, classifying each additional transaction in the current account or the financial account.
Analyze how building orientation, window placement, and prevailing wind direction influence natural ventilation in a rectangular building with windows on opposite exterior walls.
State the conditions needed for cross-ventilation to occur in a building.
Illustrate how openings on opposite exterior walls can support cross-ventilation when the building is exposed to prevailing winds.
Determine which openings act as inlets and which as outlets in the stated rectangular building, given its opposite-wall windows and the prevailing wind direction.
Critique the opposite-wall window arrangement as a means of cross-ventilating the stated rectangular building under the prevailing wind direction.
Design a natural-ventilation layout for the stated rectangular building that relates its orientation and opposite-wall window placement to the prevailing wind direction.

Analyze the relation STUDENT_COURSE(StudentID, StudentName, CourseID, CourseName, Grade), where each StudentID determines one StudentName, each CourseID determines one CourseName, and each pair (StudentID, CourseID) determines one Grade. Identify the candidate key and the functional dependencies.
Define a functional dependency and candidate key in relational database design.
Explain how the stated dependencies determine StudentName, CourseName, and Grade in the STUDENT_COURSE relation.
Apply the definition of second normal form to determine whether STUDENT_COURSE is in 2NF, identifying each partial dependency on the candidate key.
Verify whether (StudentID,CourseID) is a candidate key for STUDENT_COURSE by checking whether it determines all attributes and whether either attribute can be removed while preserving uniqueness.

Design a normalized schema that decomposes STUDENT_COURSE(StudentID, StudentName, CourseID, CourseName, Grade) into relations that remove partial dependencies on the candidate key, specifying each relation's attributes and keys.

Calculate the decimal reduction time (D-value) of a microorganism when its initial population is 10^6 cells/mL and its population decreases to 10^3 cells/mL after 6 minutes of constant-temperature treatment, assuming logarithmic microbial inactivation.
Recall the definition of the decimal reduction time (D-value) and its relationship with logarithmic microbial population reduction.
Interpret the decrease from 10^6 to 10^3 cells/mL during the 6-minute treatment as a series of decimal reductions.
Determine why the time needed for each tenfold reduction stays constant during the 6-minute treatment, and explain what this implies for the time needed to reach any lower target population.
Judge whether the reported D-value of 2 minutes is consistent with the reduction from 10^6 to 10^3 cells/mL over 6 minutes.

Develop a thermal process for the same microorganism, based on the inactivation from 10^6 to 10^3 cells/mL in 6 minutes at constant temperature, that achieves a chosen target final population, specifying the required processing time.
Calculate the software reliability over a 10-hour operating period when the system has a constant failure rate of 0.02 failures per hour, assuming an exponential reliability model.
Define software reliability and state the exponential reliability equation for a constant failure rate.
Interpret what a constant failure rate of 0.02 failures per hour implies about the probability that the software operates without failure over 10 hours.

Determine why doubling the operating period from 10 hours has the same effect on reliability as doubling the failure rate of 0.02 failures per hour, and explain what this reveals about the exponential model.
Check a reported reliability of approximately 0.819 after 10 hours against the exponential reliability model and the stated failure rate, and decide whether it is correct.

Design a reliability target for the software, starting from its constant failure rate of 0.02 failures per hour over a 10-hour operating period under the exponential reliability model, that specifies the maximum failure rate needed to reach a chosen higher reliability over the same period.

Analyze how the abstract concept of academic engagement can be operationalized using three measurable indicators: weekly study hours, class attendance percentage, and participation in classroom discussions.
Define operationalization in social research.
Explain how weekly study hours, class attendance percentage, and classroom-discussion participation can represent measurable aspects of academic engagement.

Compute an equal-weighted engagement index between 0 and 1 for a student who studies 12 hours per week (against a maximum of 20), attends 85% of classes, and participates in 3 of 10 classroom discussions, scaling each indicator to 0–1.
Assess whether the three stated indicators provide a reasonable operational representation of academic engagement, considering what each indicator measures.

Design a short survey instrument that measures academic engagement through weekly study hours, class attendance percentage, and participation in classroom discussions, specifying each item, its response scale, and how the items are combined into an engagement score.

Calculate the joint angles of a planar two-link robotic manipulator with link lengths L_1=2 m and L_2=1 m so that its end effector reaches the target position (x,y)=(2,1) m. Use the inverse-kinematics equations and identify the possible elbow configurations.
State the inverse-kinematics equations relating the link lengths, joint angles, and end-effector coordinates of a planar two-link manipulator.
Interpret how the link lengths of 2 m and 1 m and the target position (2,1) m constrain the possible joint configurations of the manipulator.
Examine the geometric relationships among the two link lengths and the target coordinates to determine why the manipulator may have more than one elbow configuration.

Verify whether the joint angles θ_1=0° and θ_2=90° place the end effector of the manipulator with link lengths 2 m and 1 m at the target position (2,1) m by substituting them into the forward-kinematics equations, and justify the conclusion.

Design a target position within the workspace of the planar two-link manipulator with L_1=2 m and L_2=1 m that has only one inverse-kinematics solution, and compare it with the two elbow configurations for the target position (2,1) m.
Compare in-situ and ex-situ conservation strategies by examining how each protects biodiversity, using a national park and a botanical garden as examples.
Recall the definitions of in-situ and ex-situ conservation.
Explain how a national park protects organisms within their natural habitats while a botanical garden conserves plant species outside their natural habitats.
Apply the distinction between in-situ and ex-situ conservation to recommend a strategy for a critically endangered plant whose only wild habitat is about to be flooded by a dam, and state why.

Can a botanical garden alone conserve the genetic diversity and ecological interactions of a threatened forest plant species as effectively as protecting its habitat in a national park? Justify your judgement.

Integrate habitat protection in a national park with a botanical-garden seed bank into a conservation plan for a threatened plant species, specifying the role of each and how plants could be reintroduced.
Calculate the reverberation time of a room with a volume of 200 m³ and a total equivalent absorption area of 50 m² using Sabine's formula, RT_60=0.161V/A.
State Sabine's formula for reverberation time and identify the room volume and total equivalent absorption area used in the equation.
Interpret how the room volume of 200 m³ and the equivalent absorption area of 50 m² set the reverberation time of the room.

Why does adding absorption to the room with a volume of 200 m³ and an absorption area of 50 m² give diminishing reductions in reverberation time? Relate your answer to the inverse relationship in Sabine's formula.
Verify whether a reported reverberation time of 0.644 seconds is correct for the room with a volume of 200 m³ and absorption area of 50 m².

Design an acoustic-treatment proposal for the room with a volume of 200 m³ and a total equivalent absorption area of 50 m² that achieves a chosen target reverberation time, specifying the additional absorption area required using Sabine's formula, RT_60=0.161V/A.

Analyze the following SQL query and its execution requirements to identify how filtering records before joining can reduce the amount of intermediate data processed.
SELECT S.StudentID, S.StudentName, E.CourseID
FROM Student S
JOIN Enrollment E ON S.StudentID = E.StudentID
WHERE S.Department = 'CSE';
Assume the Student table contains 10,000 records, of which 1,000 belong to the CSE department, and the Enrollment table contains 30,000 records.
Identify the JOIN and WHERE clauses in the given SQL query and state their respective purposes.
Explain how the condition S.Department = 'CSE' restricts the Student records considered by the given query before producing the joined result.
Modify the given SQL query to use a subquery that first selects CSE students and then joins those records with Enrollment, preserving the original output columns and join condition.

Is applying the CSE department filter before the join a worthwhile optimization for the given query, considering the 10,000 Student records, 1,000 CSE students, and 30,000 Enrollment records? Argue your answer from the intermediate result sizes.

Design an index strategy for the Student and Enrollment tables that would support the filtered join in the given query, and estimate how it reduces the records examined given 1,000 CSE students among 10,000 students and 30,000 enrollments.
Calculate the economic order quantity for a company with annual demand of 10,000 units, ordering cost of Tk. 200 per order, and annual holding cost of Tk. 5 per unit.
Write the economic order quantity formula and name each of its inputs.

Interpret the economic order quantity for an annual demand of 10,000 units, an ordering cost of Tk. 200 per order, and a holding cost of Tk. 5 per unit as the order size at which annual ordering and holding costs are equal.

Determine how the company's economic order quantity would change if the ordering cost of Tk. 200 doubled, compared with a doubling of the annual demand of 10,000 units, and explain why both have the same effect.
Validate a proposed economic order quantity of approximately 894 units for the stated demand, ordering cost, and annual holding cost.

Develop an inventory ordering plan for the company with annual demand of 10,000 units, an ordering cost of Tk. 200 per order, and an annual holding cost of Tk. 5 per unit, specifying the order quantity, the number of orders per year, and the time between orders.

Compare parliamentary and presidential systems of government by examining the relationship between the executive and legislature, the method of executive selection, and the executive's political accountability.
Name the two principal branches of government whose relationship distinguishes parliamentary from presidential systems.
Explain how the relationship between the executive and the legislature differs between parliamentary and presidential systems, including executive selection and political accountability.

Determine whether a country has a parliamentary or a presidential system if its head of government is chosen by the legislature and can be removed by a legislative vote of no confidence, using the defining features of each system.

Assess whether a parliamentary system provides stronger executive accountability than a presidential system when the governing party holds a large legislative majority, considering executive selection and accountability mechanisms.

Design a hybrid constitutional arrangement for a new state, such as a semi-presidential system, specifying executive selection, the executive–legislative relationship, and accountability mechanisms, and explain which features are drawn from each system.

Analyze the allocation of three processes with memory requirements of 100 KB, 250 KB, and 300 KB to available memory blocks of 200 KB, 300 KB, and 400 KB using the first-fit memory-allocation strategy. Determine the block assigned to each process in the given order.
Define the first-fit memory-allocation strategy and state how it searches available memory blocks for a process.
Explain how the first-fit strategy uses the available blocks of 200 KB, 300 KB, and 400 KB to allocate memory to processes requiring 100 KB, 250 KB, and 300 KB in that order.
Execute the first-fit allocation strategy for the three processes in the given order and identify the memory block assigned to each process.
Judge whether the proposed allocation of 100 KB to the 200 KB block, 250 KB to the 300 KB block, and 300 KB to the 400 KB block follows the first-fit strategy.

Design an allocation of the three processes requiring 100 KB, 250 KB, and 300 KB to the memory blocks of 200 KB, 300 KB, and 400 KB that minimizes total unused space in the allocated blocks, and compare it with the first-fit allocation.
Analyze why the central business district of a city may experience higher temperatures than its surrounding rural areas, considering surface materials, vegetation cover, and human activities.
Define the urban heat island effect.
Explain how heat-absorbing urban surfaces, limited vegetation, and human activities contribute to higher temperatures in a central business district.
Apply the three heat-island mechanisms to the stated urban conditions, stating whether each contributes to heat absorption, reduced cooling, or additional heat release.
Critique surface materials, vegetation cover, and human activities as an explanation of the higher temperatures observed in the central business district compared with surrounding rural areas.

Build a causal model of the urban heat island effect for the stated city that links surface materials, vegetation cover, and human activities to higher central-district temperatures, and identify where an intervention would break the strongest link.
Explain how soil cation exchange capacity influences the retention and availability of positively charged plant nutrients in agricultural soils.
Name positively charged plant nutrients that soil exchange sites can retain, and define cation exchange capacity.
A soil has a cation exchange capacity of 20 cmol(+)/kg and a base saturation of 60%. Calculate the quantity of exchangeable basic cations it holds.
Examine the relationship between negatively charged soil exchange sites and positively charged nutrient ions to determine how cation exchange capacity influences nutrient retention.

Recommend whether a whole season's potassium fertilizer should be applied in a single dose to a sandy soil with a cation exchange capacity of 4 cmol(+)/kg, justifying the recommendation with reference to nutrient retention and leaching.

Develop a fertilizer-management recommendation based on cation exchange capacity, explaining how the timing and quantity of positively charged nutrient applications should differ between agricultural soils with low and high cation exchange capacity.

Evaluate the effectiveness of a teacher's formative assessment approach in which students complete short quizzes after each lesson, receive feedback on incorrect answers, and use that feedback to improve their understanding before the final examination.
Define formative assessment.
Describe how short quizzes, feedback on incorrect answers, and opportunities to improve understanding support learning before the final examination.
Apply the formative-assessment cycle to decide what the teacher should do next when a lesson quiz shows that 60% of students answered the same question incorrectly.

Examine the relationship between the quizzes, feedback, and subsequent learning activities to determine how the teacher's approach supports ongoing monitoring and improvement of student understanding.
Design a formative-assessment cycle for the stated course that adds a second check after feedback to confirm whether students' understanding has improved before the final examination.

Calculate the capacitance required to improve the power factor of a single-phase load from 0.7 lagging to unity when the load consumes 5 kW at 230 V and 50 Hz. Assume the capacitor is connected in parallel with the load.
Recall the relationship between real power, power factor, and reactive power, and the formula for the reactive power supplied by a capacitor.
Explain how a parallel capacitor compensates for the lagging reactive power of the stated 5 kW load and improves its power factor from 0.7 lagging to unity.

Determine why correcting the 5 kW load from 0.7 lagging all the way to unity requires much more capacitance than correcting it to a power factor just below unity, relating this to the reactive power removed at each stage.
Verify whether a proposed capacitor rating of approximately 72.7 μF is consistent with the stated load power, initial power factor, supply voltage, and frequency.

Design a power-factor-correction scheme for the 5 kW single-phase load at 230 V and 50 Hz that corrects the power factor from 0.7 lagging to a chosen target below unity, specifying the required parallel capacitance, and compare it with the capacitance needed for unity power factor.
Calculate the support reactions of a simply supported beam of length 6 m carrying a uniformly distributed load of 4 kN/m over its entire span.
State the static equilibrium equations used to calculate the support reactions of a simply supported beam.
Explain how a uniformly distributed load of 4 kN/m over a 6 m span is converted into an equivalent concentrated load and how the beam supports resist it.
Examine the symmetry of the loading and support arrangement to determine how the total distributed load is shared between the two supports.
Verify whether the proposed reactions of 12 kN at each support satisfy both vertical-force equilibrium and moment equilibrium for the stated beam.
Design a set of concentrated loads that could replace the 4 kN/m uniformly distributed load on the 6 m simply supported beam while producing the same support reactions, and show the equivalence.
Calculate the price elasticity of demand using the percentage-change method when the price of a product increases from Tk. 50 to Tk. 60 and its quantity demanded decreases from 100 units to 80 units.
Define price elasticity of demand and state the percentage-change formula used to measure it.
Interpret what the price increase from Tk. 50 to Tk. 60 and the decrease in quantity demanded from 100 to 80 units show about consumer responsiveness.

Determine why the percentage-change method gives a different elasticity for a price fall from Tk. 60 to Tk. 50 than for the stated rise from Tk. 50 to Tk. 60, and explain how this affects the classification of demand.
Appraise a reported price elasticity of demand of −1 for the stated price and quantity changes, and judge what the result indicates about demand responsiveness.

Develop a pricing proposal for the product that uses the price elasticity obtained from the price rise from Tk. 50 to Tk. 60 and the fall in quantity demanded from 100 to 80 units to predict the effect of a further price change on total revenue and recommend a pricing direction.

Analyze whether reproducing an entire copyrighted textbook and distributing digital copies to students without the copyright holder's permission raises copyright-infringement concerns under the applicable legal framework.
List the acts that copyright protection typically controls, and define copyright.
Clarify why reproducing an entire copyrighted textbook and distributing digital copies without permission may interfere with the rights of the copyright holder.
Use the reproduction and distribution rights protected under the applicable legal framework to determine which activities in the stated textbook scenario engage each right.
Assess whether the stated reproduction and distribution of the entire textbook without permission should be treated as potential copyright infringement under the applicable legal framework.

Develop a lawful alternative plan for providing the textbook content to students, such as licensing or use within permitted exceptions, that avoids infringing the copyright holder's reproduction and distribution rights.
Use the Newton–Raphson method to approximate a root of f(x)=x^3-x-2, starting from x_0=1.5, and perform two iterations.
State the Newton–Raphson iteration formula and identify the roles of the current approximation, function value, and derivative.
Explain how the function f(x)=x^3-x-2 and its derivative determine successive root approximations starting from x_0=1.5.
Determine why the Newton–Raphson approximations for f(x)=x^3-x-2 converge rapidly from x_0=1.5, relating the speed of convergence to the size of the derivative near the root.
Is the proposed second approximation x_2≈1.52174 the correct result of two Newton–Raphson iterations starting from x_0=1.5? Verify it and state your conclusion.
Design a stopping criterion for applying the Newton–Raphson method to f(x)=x^3-x-2 from x_0=1.5, and use it to determine how many iterations are needed to reach a chosen tolerance.
Calculate the contribution margin per unit and total contribution when a company sells 2,000 units at Tk. 150 per unit and incurs variable costs of Tk. 90 per unit.
Define contribution margin per unit and total contribution, and state the formulas used to calculate them.
Interpret contribution per unit, for a product selling at Tk. 150 with a variable cost of Tk. 90, as the amount each unit adds toward fixed costs and profit.

Contrast the effect on total contribution of a given percentage rise in selling price with that of the same percentage rise in sales volume for a product selling at Tk. 150 with a variable cost of Tk. 90 and a volume of 2,000 units, and explain why they differ.
Verify whether a reported total contribution of Tk. 120,000 is correct using the stated selling price, variable cost, and sales volume.

Formulate a sales plan for the company that achieves a chosen target total contribution, using the Tk. 150 selling price, Tk. 90 variable cost per unit, and current volume of 2,000 units as the baseline.

Analyze the functional zoning of a university library containing reading areas, book stacks, administrative offices, and a service counter, considering accessibility, user movement, and relationships between spaces.
List the principal functional zones of a university library.
Explain how accessibility, user movement, and functional relationships influence the arrangement of the four library zones.
Apply adjacency principles to decide where the service counter should be located relative to the entrance, the reading areas, and the book stacks, and state the reason for each relationship.

A proposed arrangement for the library places the administrative offices at the entrance and the service counter deep inside the book stacks. Critique it in terms of user movement and functional relationships.
Design a functional-zoning layout for the stated university library that positions the reading areas, book stacks, administrative offices, and service counter to minimize conflicting user movements.

Write a C program that dynamically allocates memory for an integer array of five elements using malloc(), accepts five integer inputs, calculates their sum, and releases the allocated memory using free().
State the purposes of malloc() and free() in C.
Describe how dynamic memory allocation using malloc() allows the program to store five integer inputs and why free() is required after their sum is calculated.
Demonstrate, step by step, how the specified program allocates memory for five integers, stores the inputs, and releases the memory after summation.
Determine what would go wrong at each stage of the specified program if the malloc() call failed or free() were omitted, and identify which failure is detectable at run time.

Assess whether a C implementation that allocates space for five integers with malloc(), reads all five values, calculates their sum, checks allocation success, and calls free() correctly satisfies the stated requirements.

Calculate the probability of observing exactly three customer arrivals in a one-minute interval when the average arrival rate is two customers per minute, assuming arrivals follow a Poisson distribution.
Write the Poisson probability formula and name the roles of the average arrival rate and the number of observed events.
Interpret how an average arrival rate of two customers per minute is used to determine the probability of exactly three arrivals during a one-minute interval.

Determine why the probability of exactly three arrivals is lower than the probability of exactly two arrivals when the average rate is two customers per minute, using the ratio of successive Poisson terms.
Verify whether the reported probability of approximately 0.1804 for exactly three arrivals is correct under the stated Poisson model.

Design a staffing rule for the service point with an average arrival rate of two customers per minute that uses the Poisson distribution to set capacity so that the probability of more arrivals than planned in a one-minute interval stays below a chosen threshold.
Calculate the tex count of a yarn sample weighing 2 grams with a length of 100 metres, and interpret the resulting yarn count in terms of mass per unit length.
Define tex count and state the relationship between yarn mass and length in the tex numbering system.
Explain how the mass of 2 grams and length of 100 metres determine the fineness represented by the yarn's tex count.
Determine why the tex count would stay the same if both the mass and the length of the 2-gram, 100-metre sample were doubled, and explain what this shows about tex as a measure of fineness.
Is a reported yarn count of 20 tex correct for the sample weighing 2 grams and measuring 100 metres? Explain your verdict.

Develop a yarn-specification procedure that reports the count of the 2-gram, 100-metre yarn sample in tex, converts it to an indirect numbering system, and specifies a product label that states both values.

Analyze the alignment among a course learning outcome requiring students to evaluate database normalization choices, a teaching activity involving comparison of normalized database designs, and an assessment requiring students to justify a suitable normalization structure for a given relation.
Define constructive alignment.
Summarize how the database-normalization learning outcome, the comparison activity, and the justification-based assessment are intended to support the same learning objective.

Test a revised assessment that asks students only to define the normal forms against the principle of constructive alignment, determining whether it would still align with the outcome requiring students to evaluate database normalization choices.
Appraise the alignment of the comparison activity and the justification-based assessment with the learning outcome requiring students to evaluate database normalization choices.

Design an additional assessment task for the stated database-normalization outcome that would provide stronger evidence of students' ability to evaluate normalization choices, and explain how it aligns with the comparison activity.
Calculate the thermal efficiency of an ideal Otto cycle when the compression ratio is 8 and the specific heat ratio of the working fluid is 1.4.
State the thermal-efficiency equation for an ideal Otto cycle and identify the compression ratio and specific heat ratio.
Interpret the ideal Otto-cycle efficiency for a compression ratio of 8 and a specific heat ratio of 1.4 as the fraction of heat input converted into work.

Analyze why raising the compression ratio above 8 gives diminishing gains in ideal Otto-cycle efficiency for a specific heat ratio of 1.4, and explain how a higher specific heat ratio would change the efficiency at the same compression ratio.
Verify whether a reported ideal Otto-cycle thermal efficiency of approximately 56.5% is consistent with the stated compression ratio and specific heat ratio.

Design an engine modification that raises the ideal Otto-cycle thermal efficiency above the value obtained with a compression ratio of 8 and a specific heat ratio of 1.4, determining the compression ratio required for a chosen target efficiency.
Calculate the audit risk when inherent risk is assessed at 60%, control risk at 50%, and detection risk at 10%, using the audit risk model.
State the audit risk model and define inherent risk, control risk, and detection risk.
Describe how inherent risk of 60%, control risk of 50%, and detection risk of 10% combine in the audit risk model.

Determine why halving the detection risk of 10% halves the overall audit risk while the auditor cannot directly change the 60% inherent risk or 50% control risk, and explain the consequence for audit planning.
Validate a reported audit risk of 3% against the stated inherent risk, control risk, and detection risk assessments.

Develop an audit-plan adjustment for the engagement with inherent risk of 60% and control risk of 50% that sets the detection risk required to achieve a chosen audit risk lower than the level produced by the current 10% detection risk, and specify the substantive procedures that would achieve it.
Analyze how a decision support system can use what-if analysis to estimate the effect of changing a product's selling price on projected sales revenue, using the relationship Revenue=Price×Quantity.
State the formula relating selling price, quantity sold, and sales revenue.
Explain how what-if analysis allows a decision-maker to examine the effect of changing a product's selling price on projected sales revenue using the stated relationship.

Calculate projected sales revenue with Revenue = Price × Quantity when the price is Tk. 250 and quantity is 1,200 units, and when the price is raised to Tk. 275 with projected quantity falling to 1,050 units.

A what-if analysis concludes that raising the price from Tk. 250 to Tk. 275 increases revenue because each unit earns more, even though projected quantity falls from 1,200 to 1,050 units. Is this conclusion sound? Justify your judgement with the revenue relationship.
Design a what-if analysis model for the stated decision support task that tests several price levels with their projected quantities and identifies the price that maximizes projected sales revenue.

Calculate the discharge through a horizontal venturimeter when the inlet diameter is 10 cm, the throat diameter is 5 cm, and the pressure difference between the inlet and throat is 12 kPa. Assume water density is 1000 kg/m^3 and the venturimeter has a discharge coefficient of 0.98.
State the discharge equation for a venturimeter and identify the roles of inlet area, throat area, pressure difference, fluid density, and discharge coefficient.
Explain how the difference between inlet and throat areas produces a pressure difference that can be used to determine discharge through the horizontal venturimeter.

Determine why the discharge through the venturimeter depends on the ratio of throat to inlet diameter as well as on the 12 kPa pressure difference, and identify how the discharge would change if the pressure difference were quadrupled.
Verify whether a reported discharge of approximately 0.0143 m^3/s is consistent with the stated venturimeter dimensions, pressure difference, water density, and discharge coefficient.

Design a modified throat diameter for the horizontal venturimeter with a 10 cm inlet so that the discharge obtained with the 5 cm throat and 12 kPa pressure difference would produce a larger, chosen pressure difference, using the stated water density of 1000 kg/m^3 and discharge coefficient.
Analyze how skill requirements, responsibility, effort, and working conditions can influence the relative worth of different jobs within an organization using a point-factor job evaluation approach.
Name the factors typically used in a point-factor job evaluation approach.
Discuss why a point-factor approach considers multiple job-related factors when determining the relative worth of different positions.

Apply a point-factor scheme that weights skill at 40%, responsibility at 30%, effort at 20%, and working conditions at 10% to calculate the weighted score of a job rated 4, 3, 2, and 5 on those factors, each on a 1–5 scale.
Is a job evaluation that considers skill, responsibility, effort, and working conditions a sound basis for comparing the relative worth of organizational positions? Defend your view.
Construct a point-factor job evaluation framework that assigns weights and level definitions to skill, responsibility, effort, and working conditions, and justify the weighting.

Compare the executive–legislative relationship in parliamentary government with the principle of collective ministerial responsibility, explaining how these features shape executive accountability to the legislature.
Recall the meaning of collective ministerial responsibility.
Use the principle of collective ministerial responsibility to interpret a parliamentary situation in which a cabinet must publicly support a collectively agreed government decision.
Examine how the relationship between the executive and legislature interacts with collective ministerial responsibility to create mechanisms of political accountability.
Critique collective ministerial responsibility as a basis for executive accountability to the legislature, considering the relationship between cabinet unity and legislative scrutiny.

Develop a set of accountability procedures for a parliamentary system, such as question time and confidence votes, specifying how each enforces collective ministerial responsibility to the legislature.
Calculate the material cost variance when the standard quantity is 500 kg at Tk. 20 per kg and the actual quantity used is 520 kg at Tk. 22 per kg.
State the material cost variance formula and define standard cost and actual cost in material variance analysis.
Explain how differences between the standard quantity and price and the actual quantity and price contribute to material cost variance.
Examine the separate effects of the quantity difference and price difference on the material cost variance using the stated standard and actual figures.
Verify whether a reported material cost variance of Tk. 1,440 adverse is correct using the stated standard quantity, standard price, actual quantity, and actual price.

Develop a corrective-action plan for the material cost variance arising from a standard of 500 kg at Tk. 20 per kg and actual usage of 520 kg at Tk. 22 per kg, separating the price and usage causes and proposing measures for each.
Analyze how particle size, gas velocity, and centrifugal action influence the collection efficiency of a cyclone separator used to remove particulate matter from an industrial gas stream.
Recall the separating principle on which a cyclone separator operates.
Illustrate how centrifugal action separates suspended particles from an industrial gas stream inside a cyclone separator.
Predict the qualitative effect on particle collection when the particle size increases while the gas velocity and cyclone configuration remain unchanged.

Is increasing gas velocity alone a sufficient strategy for improving cyclone collection efficiency? Evaluate this view, considering its relationship with centrifugal action and the other stated factors.
Design a cyclone-separator specification for a chosen particle-size range, specifying the gas velocity and geometry that would achieve effective centrifugal collection, and justify each choice.
Apply the concept of operationalization to convert the abstract variable of academic engagement into measurable indicators for a university student survey.
Define operationalization and distinguish an abstract research variable from a measurable indicator.
Explain why academic engagement must be translated into measurable indicators before it can be investigated through a university student survey.
Examine the relationship between the abstract concept of academic engagement and its potential measurable dimensions to distinguish the construct from the indicators used to represent it.

A proposed set of survey indicators measures academic engagement using students' family income, distance from campus, and age. Assess whether these indicators adequately represent academic engagement rather than unrelated student characteristics.
Develop an operational definition of academic engagement for a university student survey, specifying measurable indicators and explaining how each represents the abstract variable.

Apply a proportional–integral–derivative (PID) controller to a robot motor-control system with proportional gain K_p=2, integral gain K_i=0.5, derivative gain K_d=1, and error signal e(t)=3, assuming the error derivative is 0.4 and the accumulated error is 2. State the PID controller output equation and identify the proportional, integral, and derivative contributions.

Separate the proportional, integral, and derivative contributions to the controller output for the stated gains and error conditions, identify which dominates, and explain how the balance would shift as the error approaches zero.
Check a reported controller output of 7.4 against the stated gains, error, accumulated error, and error derivative, and decide whether it is correct.

Design modified PID gains for the robot motor-control system that achieve a chosen target controller output under the stated conditions (e(t)=3, error derivative 0.4, accumulated error 2), starting from K_p=2, K_i=0.5, and K_d=1.
Calculate the time required to achieve a 6-log reduction in a microbial population when the D-value at the processing temperature is 2 minutes, assuming constant processing conditions.
Define the decimal reduction time (D-value).
Interpret how a D-value of 2 minutes relates processing time to successive one-log reductions in the microbial population.
Determine why the time for a 6-log reduction is six times the D-value of 2 minutes regardless of the starting population, and explain what this implies for heavily contaminated products.
Verify whether a reported processing time of 12 minutes is consistent with achieving a 6-log reduction when the D-value is 2 minutes under constant processing conditions.

Design a thermal process for the product with a D-value of 2 minutes at the processing temperature that delivers the required 6-log reduction with a chosen safety margin, specifying the holding time and how it changes if the target log reduction is increased.
Analyze the suitability of pitched and flat roof systems for a university building in a hot, humid, high-rainfall climate, considering rainwater drainage, maintenance access, and usable roof space.
Name the two main roof-system types used in building construction.
Explain how roof form can influence rainwater drainage, maintenance access, and the availability of usable roof space in a hot, humid, high-rainfall climate.
Apply the three stated considerations to the pitched and flat roof options for the university building, stating the implication of each roof for drainage, maintenance access, and usable roof space.
Assess which of the two roof systems is more suitable for the stated university building by weighing rainwater drainage, maintenance access, and usable roof space.
Design a hybrid roof for the stated university building that combines pitched and flat sections to provide drainage, maintenance access, and usable roof space, and justify the arrangement.

Apply the write-ahead logging recovery procedure to a database transaction that updates account A from Tk. 5,000 to Tk. 4,000 and account B from Tk. 3,000 to Tk. 4,000. State the purpose of a commit record in transaction logging and identify the role of before-images and after-images in the given log records.

Examine the sequence of log records and the crash position to distinguish the recovery requirements for transaction T1 from those of an uncommitted transaction.
Appraise the recovery decision to redo transaction T1 and retain account balances of Tk. 4,000 each in light of the commit record and the stated crash condition.

Construct a recovery scenario for transaction T1 in which the system crashes before the <COMMIT T1> record is written to the log, and specify the recovery actions and the resulting values of accounts A and B.

Explain how the limit test for chloride detects chloride impurities in a pharmaceutical substance by comparing the turbidity produced by the test solution with that of a standard chloride solution under the same conditions.
Identify the reagent commonly used to produce turbidity in the chloride limit test and state the purpose of the standard chloride solution.
Determine whether a pharmaceutical sample passes the chloride limit test when it produces greater turbidity than the standard chloride solution under identical test conditions.
Analyze why the chloride limit test compares turbidity with a standard rather than measuring chloride directly, and identify the condition whose violation would invalidate the comparison.

Design a laboratory procedure for the chloride limit test, specifying the preparation of the test and standard solutions, the conditions for turbidity development, and the decision rule for their comparison.
Calculate the cycle length of a fixed-time traffic signal using Webster's formula when the total lost time per cycle is 12 seconds and the sum of critical flow ratios is 0.75.
State Webster's optimum cycle-length formula and define total lost time and the sum of critical flow ratios.
Explain how total lost time of 12 seconds and a sum of critical flow ratios of 0.75 influence the optimum cycle length calculated using Webster's formula.
Determine why the Webster cycle length increases sharply as the sum of critical flow ratios of 0.75 approaches one, while it rises only linearly with the 12-second lost time.
Verify whether a proposed optimum cycle length of 84 seconds is consistent with Webster's formula and the stated traffic-signal parameters.

Design a two-phase signal timing plan for the intersection with a total lost time of 12 seconds per cycle and a sum of critical flow ratios of 0.75, allocating effective green time to phases with critical flow ratios of your choice that sum to 0.75, using Webster's optimum cycle length.

Calculate the government expenditure multiplier in a simple economy when the marginal propensity to consume is 0.8 and the marginal propensity to save is 0.2, using the expenditure multiplier formula.
Recall the government expenditure multiplier formula and the definitions of the marginal propensity to consume and to save.
Explain how an MPC of 0.8 and an MPS of 0.2 determine the size of the expenditure multiplier in the simple economy.
Analyze why the successive rounds of spending in the simple economy shrink by the factor 0.8 each time, and determine why their total equals the reciprocal of the marginal propensity to save of 0.2.
Is a reported government expenditure multiplier of 5 consistent with the stated MPC and MPS values and the simple-economy multiplier formula? Explain your verdict.

Design a fiscal-stimulus proposal for the economy with a marginal propensity to consume of 0.8 and a marginal propensity to save of 0.2 that achieves a chosen target increase in equilibrium income, determining the required change in government expenditure.

Analyze whether a seller's statement that a used vehicle has never been involved in an accident, despite knowing that it was previously damaged in a collision, may constitute misrepresentation when the buyer relies on that statement to purchase the vehicle.
Recall the definition of misrepresentation in contract law.
Discuss why a seller's knowingly false statement about a vehicle's accident history may influence a buyer's decision to enter into a transaction.
Apply the general elements of misrepresentation to the stated vehicle-sale scenario, identifying the statement, its falsity, the seller's knowledge, and the buyer's reliance.
